bounded_statement: For the selected result only: the reported rejection of the no-preference null (exact binomial test, 15 of 20 pooled trials on the marked arm, two-sided p = 0.0414, alpha = 0.05) is obtained by entering all four trials from each of the five colonies as 20 independent Bernoulli observations, even though data-description.md declares colony_id as the independent-unit column and states that same-colony tests share nest, forager pool, and extract batch. With only 5 independent units, the pooled test overstates the effective sample size; at the declared unit level 4 of 5 colonies show a marked-arm majority (two-sided sign test p = 0.375), so the significance claim at alpha = 0.05 is not supported by an analysis respecting the declared independent unit. This is bounded to the supplied files and the selected result; it does not claim the underlying biological effect is absent.

counterevidence_considered.description: The data description also defines one trial as one row, and each row records a genuinely distinct release of a forager, so the pooling is not literal duplication of records; the report is also fully transparent that all 20 trials were pooled. This mitigates concerns of fabrication or hidden methodology but does not restore the binomial test's independence assumption across repeated entries of the same declared independent unit.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: one trial = one row; pooling openly disclosed

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the finding three ways. (1) Recomputed the pooled statistic from the raw CSV: 15 of 20 rows are marked, and the exact two-sided binomial p is 2 x 21700/2^20 = 0.0414, confirming the code and report are internally consistent, so the issue is not a computation error. (2) Re-ran the inference at the declared independent-unit level: per-colony marked counts are 4/4, 4/4, 3/4, 3/4, 1/4, so 4 of 5 colonies show a marked majority; a two-sided sign test on 5 colonies gives p = 2 x 6/32 = 0.375, so the alpha = 0.05 rejection disappears when each colony enters the procedure once — the significance is therefore attributable to the repeated per-colony entries rather than robust to them. (3) Searched workflow/analysis.py for any use of colony_id, per-colony aggregation, or clustering/mixed-model adjustment that could justify row-level pooling; there is none — colony_id is read but never referenced in the analysis. All three checks left the issue standing.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py performs no per-colony aggregation or clustering adjustment: summarise() counts successes across all 20 rows and main() passes the pooled counts directly to scipy.stats.binomtest(n_marked, n_trials, 0.5), whose exact null distribution treats each of the n_trials rows as an independent observation. Because each colony_id contributes four rows, each authorized independent unit enters the row-independent binomial procedure four times, inflating the effective sample size from 5 to 20 and producing the p = 0.0414 rejection reported in results/report.md.
